items.title: Man, 66, found dead in bathroom after Kota Bharu house fire
items.summary: Kota Bharu Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Mohd Ridzuan Baharudin said the victim, Kang Choo Hock, was found in the bathroom at 9.37pm and was confirmed dead at the scene. He said they received an emergency call through NG999 at 8.43pm before fire engines arrived at the scene, about five kilometres from the Kota Bharu Fire and Rescue Station, at 8.52pm. He added that the operation involved 35 personnel from the Kota Bharu, Kota Darul Naim and Pengkalan Chepa Fire and Rescue stations, as well as three Fire and Rescue Tender vehicles and a water tanker.

items.title: CPO prices seen at RM4,400-RM4,600 on tighter supply
items.summary: However, elevated Malaysian palm oil inventories could cap near-term gains, with stocks expected to rise another 5.3 per cent month-on-month (MoM) to 2.98 million tonnes in September. Malaysian palm oil inventories rose 7.5 per cent MoM and 28.2 per cent year-on-year (YoY) to 2.82 million tonnes in August, exceeding CIMB Securities' forecast of 2.68 million tonnes and consensus expectations of between 2.76 million and 2.78 million tonnes. CIMB Securities said exports fell 7.5 per cent MoM and 2.4 per cent YoY to 1.29 million tonnes, likely reflecting weaker demand amid elevated CPO prices.

items.title: Cargo vessel fire at east China shipyard kills 25
items.summary: BEIJING: Twenty-five people died in a fire aboard a foreign cargo vessel undergoing repairs at a state-owned shipyard in the eastern Chinese city of Qingdao on Thursday, state media reported. The fire broke out at about 11.15am (0315 GMT) at the Qingdao Beihai shipyard during repair and inspection works, state-run Xinhua said. The blaze was extinguished by early afternoon, state media said.

items.title: ‘You are not alone’: Deputy minister urges domestic violence victims to seek help after Malaysian mother killed in Perth
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 11 — Domestic violence should not be treated as a private matter or endured alone, as it is a serious form of violence that must not be normalised under any circumstances, said Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying. She said domestic violence can have a profound impact not only on victims, but also on children, families and the wellbeing of society as a whole. Lim said efforts to prevent violence, protect victims and ensure they receive the necessary support and access to appropriate assistance must be a shared responsibility.

items.title: Ringgit opens slightly lower against greenback on stronger US economic data
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened slightly lower against the US dollar on Friday, weighed by stronger-than-expected US economic data which supported the greenback. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US producer price index (PPI) rose more than expected to 5.4 per cent year-on-year in August, up from 4.8 per cent in July, versus consensus estimates of 5.3 per cent. Meanwhile, core PPI also increased to 4.6 per cent from 4.3 per cent previously.

items.title: Serian records country's highest API reading at 195
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Serian recorded the country's highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 195 as of 8am today, with 15 areas nationwide registering unhealthy air quality amid the ongoing transboundary haze. In Sabah, Kota Kinabalu recorded an unhealthy API reading of 150, while Labuan recorded 133. Meanwhile, 48 stations recorded moderate API readings.

items.title: Anwar tells PKR to close ranks, gear up for GE16
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — PKR must continue to strengthen the administration of the Federal and State Governments to ensure that implemented policies provide tangible benefits to the people, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar, who is also the PKR president, said the party must also move with the strength of all its members, close ranks, and embrace the support of all layers of society so that PKR remains close to the pulse and aspirations of the people. Earlier, he held a brief meeting with the Sabah PKR State Leadership Council here to discuss various current issues and the importance of the welfare of the people in the state.

items.title: From Maggi noodles to Thums Up: How India became dependent on cheap packaged food
items.summary: NEW DELHI: India's proposal to put health warning labels on some food products has sparked a nationwide debate over how the country came to rely on cheap packaged food while companies sold more nutritious versions of the same brands in other markets. With an income per household well below the global average, Indians are keen consumers of cheap food products such as Nestle-owned Maggi instant noodles and Coca-Cola Co's Thums Up — giving big food manufacturers a huge market with little pressure to apply the food standards they adopt in many other countries. Fast-growing market India's packaged food market grew to $137.25 billion this year, from $129.18 billion in 2025, and is projected to reach $238.83 billion by 2034, according to research firm IMARC Group.

items.title: 1MDB taskforce backs S$1b claim against DBS over Jho Low-linked accounts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — The 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) Asset Recovery Taskforce said claims for damages filed by four companies’ court-appointed liquidators suing DBS Bank are linked to accounts opened by Jho Low associate Eric Tan. In a statement, the taskforce said based on the statement of claim filed, the five accounts in question were opened with DBS in 2013. It said the account opening papers for all four companies named Tan Kim Loong, better known as Eric Tan, as their sole beneficial owner.

items.title: Trump says he does not regret Iran war despite impact it may have on midterm elections
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump said he did not regret going to war against Iran despite the impact the conflict may have on the November US midterm elections. You can always question yourself a little bit," Trump said in an interview with Fox News host Laura Ingraham when asked if he regretted the Iran war due to the impact it may have on the elections. Trump has cited weakening Iran's nuclear capabilities as one of his war objectives.

items.title: Gaza official says 22,000 Palestinians need treatment abroad, wants evacuation of 1,000 daily
items.summary: GAZA CITY: The head of the Gaza government media office, Ismail al-Thawabteh, told Anadolu Ajansi on Thursday that 22,000 wounded and sick Palestinians in the Gaza Strip urgently need to travel abroad for treatment. His remarks came in response to Israeli figures on Palestinian movement through Gaza crossings since a ceasefire took effect last October. The Times of Israel news site earlier cited Israel's Border Crossings Authority, which said around 10,500 people had left Gaza since the ceasefire took effect, according to Anadolu.

items.title: Vance takes spotlight as Republicans close Trump-heavy convention
items.summary: DALLAS: US Republicans returned to the stage Thursday to close their midterm convention, still betting that Donald Trump's political magnetism can overcome grim election forecasts – while giving Vice President JD Vance a prime-time showcase as a potential heir. Trump will dominate the finale of the two-day gathering, delivering closing remarks after Vance's keynote address at the American Airlines Centre in downtown Dallas. Trump dramatically raised the stakes in his opening night keynote Wednesday, promising a US$5,000 "Trump dividend" to every American adult if Republicans retain both chambers of Congress in November.

items.title: When people leave
items.summary: EMPLOYEES come and go. People join organisations, develop their skills, build relationships, pursue ambitions and eventually, some decide it is time to move on. For business owners, however, an employee leaving can create a very real operational challenge.

items.title: Malaysia's revived nuclear ambition could see first plant in 2040s [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's decades-old nuclear power ambition is returning to the table as rising electricity demand from data centres and volatile fossil fuel prices revive the case for a source of firm, low-carbon power. Malaysia has restarted its Phase 1 early-stage assessment under the International Atomic Energy Agency's (IAEA) framework, with Malaysia Programme Office for Power Electricity Reform Corp (MyPOWER) tasked with coordinating the process. CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd analyst Muhammad Afif Zulkaplly said the renewed assessment is timely as conversations over Malaysia establishing its own nuclear power plant have resurfaced among industry players.

items.title: Musk threatens legal action over documentary
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Elon Musk's lawyers put the makers of a new four-hour documentary about the multibillionaire on formal legal notice days before its premiere, warning that the film defames him. The Sept 3 letter from attorney Alex Spiro, addressed to a producer at Alex Gibney's Jigsaw Productions, accuses the Oscar-winning documentarian of building "Musk" around a predetermined conclusion. It also says Gibney refused to fact-check the film with the world's richest man or the people close to him.

items.title: Maduro's wife seeks release from detention, citing ill health
items.summary: NEW YORK: The wife of Venezuela's deposed leader Nicolas Maduro, both of whom face drug trafficking charges in the United States, has requested to be released from New York detention and placed under house arrest, citing heart problems. The authoritarian Maduro, 63, and Flores were seized by the United States during a raid in Caracas and have been detained since Jan 3. They stand accused of helping smuggle tonnes of cocaine into the United States.

items.title: Diana's 'revenge dress' to go up for auction in New York
items.summary: NEW YORK: Princess Diana's famous "revenge dress" that she wore on the evening that then-Prince Charles made a public admission of adultery is to be auctioned in New York in December. "Princess Diana turned the dress into one of the most powerful messages she ever made, during one of the most scrutinized and emotionally charged episodes of her life," said Morgane Halimi of Sotheby's, which announced the upcoming sale on Thursday. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Trump administration proposes waiving grace period for H-1B holders after job loss
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The Trump administration has proposed eliminating a 60-day grace period that allows certain immigrants, including skilled workers on H-1B visas, to stay in the United States and find a new sponsor after losing their job, according to a government notice posted online Thursday. His administration has also introduced higher visa fees for skilled workers and recently paused immigrant visa appointments at US missions around the world while it implements a new training programme. Companies impacted by the change could see some disruption, DHS wrote in its proposal, but it said the jobs could go to American workers instead.

items.title: Zahid: Umno to seek strategic partners ahead of GE16 [WATCH]
items.summary: As the party charts its way forward, president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has also sought to distinguish Umno's emphasis on Malay unity from what critics have described as identity politics, stressing that the party recognises Malaysia's multiracial character. In an exclusive interview with Media Prima Bhd amid the Umno general assembly, Zahid outlined Umno's approach to GE16, its evolving political partnerships and efforts to remain relevant as it looks towards the next decade. As we approach the next decade, people will ask whether Umno remains relevant.

items.title: Malaysia wants to be an AI nation by 2030 — what does that mean for Malaysians?
items.summary: Now, the government wants to take that further, aiming to make Malaysia an “AI nation” by 2030. National AI Action Plan 2026 to 2030 The National AI Action Plan 2026–2030 is the government’s roadmap for increasing the responsible adoption and development of AI. TalentCorp has identified emerging roles including AI engineers, AI and machine-learning application engineers, AI integration engineers, data scientists, data engineers, AI auditors and AI ethicists.

items.title: US slaps new sanctions on networks aiding Iran's proxies in Middle East
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US government announced new sanctions on Thursday against firms and individuals that it says are aiding Hizbollah and other Iranian proxies in the Middle East as it intensified its campaign to isolate Iran economically. Thursday's actions by Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control hit entities and individuals that support Kata'ib Hizbollah, an Iraqi Shia paramilitary group under the command of the IRGC, and Hizbollah, a Lebanese Shia party, Treasury said in a statement. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: George Town wins silver for smoke-free efforts
items.summary: GEORGE Town has won silver at the second Asean Smoke-free Awards, in recognition of its achievements in implementing and enforcing smoke-free policies to protect public health. The award was presented at the 17th Asean Health Ministers' Meeting here yesterday. The initiative is led by Laos under the Asean Health Cluster 1, in cooperation with the Southeast Asia Tobacco Control Alliance (SEATCA) and the Asean Secretariat.

items.title: Putin arrives in India for BRICS summit coloured by wars
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in the Indian capital on Friday ahead of an 11-member BRICS summit set to be dominated by wars in the Middle East and Ukraine, as well as economic challenges. Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian were due to hold talks with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while Chinese President Xi Jinping was also expected to meet him on the sidelines of the two-day meeting, according to Indian diplomatic sources. Putin arrived at Palam Air Force Station in New Delhi, where he was greeted by India's Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh, according to footage broadcast by Russia's Ria Novosti news agency.

items.title: Malaysia's first NCD clinic in food court to open in Johor
items.summary: THE Johor Baru City Council (MBJB) is opening the country's first non-communicable disease (NCD) clinic in a food court at the Medan Niaga Kampung Melayu Majidee. State Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said the facility would take up six lots and handle NCD follow-up services from the Majidee public clinic. "Once completed, it is expected to be the first NCD clinic in Malaysia to operate from a food court, serving about 200 patients daily," he said.

items.title: Tremor recorded as Israel says Hizbollah tunnels destroyed in south Lebanon
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Israel said Thursday it demolished key tunnels built by the Iran-backed Hizbollah group beneath the strategic Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon, triggering a 4.1 magnitude tremor. AFP journalists in the area heard several explosions. AFP journalists in south Lebanon also said they heard "huge explosions" on Thursday evening.

items.title: Samsung won't Fold over easily to Apple
items.summary: SEOUL: Samsung launched a campaign promoting its foldable phones, highlighting hardware advantage and early lead in the segment as it seeks to fend off a major challenge from Apple. On Wednesday, Apple unveiled the US$1,999 Duo, a foldable iPhone aimed at shaking up a category long dominated by Samsung and Chinese companies such as Huawei, whose devices have struggled to move beyond a niche audience. Apple adopted the passport-shaped design Samsung Electronics unveiled less than two months ago with the Galaxy Z Fold 8, which is priced at US$1,899 and uses Alphabet's Gemini artificial intelligence.

items.title: Several dead in Dutch coach crash in Switzerland
items.summary: GENEVA: Several people were killed and injured when a coach carrying Dutch tourists in eastern Switzerland crashed, police said on Thursday. The coach hit a safety barrier before overturning and plunging down an embankment, a local police spokesman told Swiss media. "Several people died in the coach crash in Susch.

items.title: Hasina's daughter quits as WHO regional lead
items.summary: SAIMA Wazed, the World Health Organisation's (WHO) Southeast Asia head and daughter of ousted Bangladeshi prime minister Sheikh Hasina, resigned on Wednesday, according to her resignation letter seen by Reuters, following fraud investigations by the United Nations agency and Bangladeshi authorities. Many of Hasina's allies face criminal charges, including for alleged corruption in Bangladesh, or live in self-imposed exile like Hasina. Wazed has denied the allegations.

items.title: What to know about Trump's US$5,000 'dividend' pledge
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump has promised US$5,000 to every American adult if Republicans retain control of the House of Representatives and the Senate in November's midterm elections. Trump has made similar pledges in the past which never came about, including promising Americans US$2,000 checks from tariff revenues and US$5,000 checks from savings made from drastic federal job cuts. Restricting the payments to US citizens would reduce that figure to about US$1.27 trillion.

items.title: White House says it will send US$500 Obamacare refunds to nearly a million Americans
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The White House said on Thursday it will send US$500 to nearly one million Americans in 30 states who are enrolled in Obamacare health insurance plans, payments it described as refunds for overcharges. It said "user fees" passed on to consumers in the form of higher premiums by the administration of President Joe Biden were in excess of what was needed to run the federal exchange, or Healthcare.gov. Obamacare plans, created by Democratic President Barack Obama's signature Affordable Care Act, offer subsidies based on income.

items.title: Iran likely to reverse-engineer captured US underwater drone
items.summary: IRAN'S capture of a US military underwater drone gives Teheran an opportunity to study and potentially reverse engineer the vessel, delivering a setback for the Pentagon and drone maker Anduril. The US military and Anduril have downplayed the significance of the drone falling into Iranian hands. After Iran captured an RQ-170 Sentinel stealth reconnaissance drone in 2011, then-President Barack Obama publicly asked Teheran to return the aircraft.

items.title: Anwar: PKR must strengthen federal, state administrations ahead of GE16
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim says PKR must continue strengthening the administration of the federal and state governments to ensure policies deliver tangible benefits to the people. Anwar, who is also PKR president, said the party must move with unity, close ranks, and embrace support across society to remain close to the pulse and aspirations of the people. He stressed Sabah PKR will remain a major force carrying the people's voice and advancing reform.

items.title: Japan seeks change to new UN world map over Russia 'misconception'
items.summary: TOKYO: Japan said on Thursday it had asked for the revision of a new world map adopted by the United Nations because it made the disputed Kuril islands appear to belong to Russia. The UN General Assembly voted on Friday to adopt the new map, which makes the African continent larger while also shrinking North America and Europe, drawing condemnation from the United States. Top Japanese government spokesman Minoru Kihara said the new map – known as the Equal Earth cartographic projection – "contained a depiction contradicting the Japanese government's position."

items.title: Indonesian wildfires cause respiratory infections to double in a week, health ministry says
items.summary: JAKARTA: Respiratory infections caused by hazardous wildfire pollution in Indonesia have more than doubled in just over a week, data from the country's health ministry showed on Thursday. Fires have been blazing across vast stretches of forest and peatland throughout the Indonesian archipelago, causing hazardous emissions to surge, particularly in the hardest-hit provinces on the islands of Sumatra and Borneo. More than 12.5 million people have been exposed to haze caused by fires across seven provinces, said Widyawati, who goes by one name.

items.title: S$1bil Singapore claim against DBS linked to Jho Low associate Eric Tan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 1MDB Asset Recovery Taskforce says claims filed in Singapore against DBS Bank are tied to accounts opened by Eric Tan, a Malaysian associate of fugitive financier Low Taek Jho, better known as Jho Low. Liquidators of four companies — BlackRock Commodities (Global) Ltd, Platinum Global Luxury Services Ltd, Affinity Equity International Partners and TKIL Global Investments Ltd — have filed a claim exceeding S$1 billion in the Singapore High Court. Tan acted as Jho Low's proxy.

items.title: PM Anwar to meet Modi, Putin and other leaders during Brics Summit in New Delhi
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 10 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is set to engage in high-level bilateral meetings with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin during his working visit to the Indian capital for the 18th BRICS Summit this weekend. “Besides Modi and Putin, the Prime Minister will also meet Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed on the sidelines of the Summit. Malaysia is participating in the BRICS Leaders’ Summit in New Delhi as a BRICS Partner Country.

items.title: Three suspects arrested in Alam Megah murder case, police thank public for vital leads
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 10 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have arrested three of seven suspects wanted to assist investigations into the Alam Megah murder in Section 28, here last month. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the suspects, all locals in their 20s and 40s, were arrested between Sept 4 and 7 following leads from members of the public after their photographs were made public last Friday. Meanwhile, commenting on public calls for the proposed construction of a new police station in Puncak Alam following three successful operations to dismantle drug laboratories in the area, Shazeli said there are several key factors that need to be taken into consideration.

items.title: Op Fella widens: MACC wants prison access to question ex‑Felda chairman on asset deals
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 10 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will seek the cooperation of the Malaysian Prison Department to record the statement of a former Felda chairman currently serving a prison sentence to assist its investigation into the assets and investments of Felda Investment Corporation (FIC). MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the statement needed to be recorded due to a link between the purchase of certain assets and FIC investments currently under investigation. Abd Halim said seven investigation papers had been opened to date under ‘Op Fella’, while statements from 29 witnesses had been recorded in investigations into alleged corruption involving asset purchases and investments by Felda and FIC.

items.title: Judges Alice Loke and Elaine Yap take oaths, marking new appointments in Malaysian judiciary
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 10 — High Court Judge Alice Loke Yee Ching today took her oath of office and allegiance as a Court of Appeal judge. Judicial Commissioner Elaine Yap Chin Gaik, meanwhile, took her oath of office and allegiance as a High Court judge. She was appointed a High Court Judicial Commissioner on July 10, 2020.

items.title: Super El Niño to torch Malaysia next March, MetMalaysia warns heat soaring past 40°C
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) expects temperatures in several parts of the country to exceed 40 degrees Celsius next year, driven by a Super El Niño phenomenon forecast to reach its strongest intensity on record. “The highest daily temperature ever recorded in the country was 40.1 degrees Celsius in Chuping, Perlis, during the Super El Niño phenomenon of 1997/1998. “Given that this phenomenon is forecast to be stronger than previous episodes, compounded by global warming, temperatures can surpass that record and reach 40.5 or even 41 degrees Celsius,” he said during an appearance on Bernama Radio’s Fokus 30 programme titled Super El Niño: Kesan Kepada Negara (Super El Niño: Impact on the Nation), today.

items.title: MACC to charge ex‑minister Monday over Tabung Haji RCI, probe assets in Saudi Arabia
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 10 — A former minister will be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court next Monday as part of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) probe arising from the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). Speaking at a special press conference at the MACC headquarters today, Abd Halim said the former minister was also linked to assets in Saudi Arabia. He said five people had been charged so far in the TH RCI probe: a former deputy general manager of construction and a former security and health manager at TH Properties Sdn Bhd, a former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman, Alam Maritim Sdn Bhd’s chief executive officer, and a former TH chief operating officer.

items.title: Police record 12 witness statements after RM2.91m armed gang robbery at Jalan Ampang condo
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Police have recorded the statements of 12 witnesses to assist investigations into an armed gang robbery at a luxury condominium in Jalan Ampang here, involving losses of RM2.91 million. In a statement today, Wangsa Maju police chief ACP Annas Sulaiman said they are still working to identify all the suspects involved. Those with information on the incident are urged to contact the Wangsa Maju district police control centre at 03-9289 9222, Kuala Lumpur police hotline at 03-2115 9999, or any nearby police station.

items.title: Petronas-Petros deal could face ‘Tabung Haji’ reckoning in future, warns expert
items.summary: Walter Sandosam said the political circumstances surrounding any agreement could later come under scrutiny, even if it is defended today as a practical solution. “Petronas-Petros could become a future accountability issue if a settlement is seen as political compromise rather than national-interest decision,” he said. “This creates space for political horse-trading,” he said.

items.title: Farmer shot dead outside family member’s rented house in Banting
items.summary: Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the victim died at the scene after being hit by several shots in the incident between 10.30 pm and 11 pm. “Police received information about the incident at about 11.15 pm. Following the incident, police detained a local man in his 20s to 30s around the Banting area late last night.

items.title: No indication of volcanic ash entering Malaysian airspace, says MetMalaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — There are no indications that toxic volcanic ash from an eruption in Indonesia is moving across Malaysian airspace, as recently claimed on social media. Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said current monitoring showed that volcanic ash, including from Gunung Anak Krakatau, was moving towards the Indian Ocean northwest of Sumatra, rather than towards Malaysia. “Monitoring shows that the ash is moving towards open waters, not towards the peninsula, Sabah or Sarawak.

items.title: Rosmah’s solar graft case: High Court to hear fresh evidence from key witness on Sept 17
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The High Court today set September 17 to hear additional evidence from the star prosecution witness, Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah, in Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor’s solar hybrid project graft trial. Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin fixed the date after Rosmah’s counsel, Datuk Jagjit Singh, told the court that the Court of Appeal had allowed Rosmah’s application to adduce additional evidence in her appeal and directed that the additional evidence be recorded by the High Court. If not, we will proceed as ordered by the Court of Appeal.

items.title: PAS at Umno assembly: Friendly visit or ‘preview’ of next election?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — When PAS delegates began arriving at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur last night for Umno’s annual assembly this week, the gesture drew more than polite greetings from party members. For some Umno delegates, the presence of PAS delegates was a sign that the idea of Malay-Muslim unity was gaining ground again. For others, it was a matter of returning a courtesy after Umno representatives attended PAS’s muktamar last week.

items.title: Four Chinese nationals face kidnapping charge after Singaporean allegedly held for RM3.28m ransom
items.summary: BALIK PULAU, Sept 10 — Four Chinese nationals were charged at the Sessions Court here today with kidnapping a Singaporean man in July and demanding a ransom of SGD1 million (about RM3.28 million). The accused, Liu Ting Jun, 46; Huang Jian, 39; Wang Hao Yu, 32; and Guan Siqi, 24, the only woman among them, however, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read to them in Mandarin before Judge Ahzal Fariz Ahmad Khairuddin. According to the charge sheet, the accused, as well as two others still at large and another two individuals who have since died, are accused of jointly abducting and wrongfully confining Quek Aik Teng at the Penang International Airport in Bayan Lepas at 4.15 pm on July 26.

items.title: Drug syndicates use public as mules to smuggle cannabis to Europe, says Bukit Aman
items.summary: BACHOK, Sept 10 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have found that drug trafficking syndicates operating by air to Europe frequently use members of the public as drug mules, particularly to transport cannabis flowers, which are in high demand on the continent. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department Director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said, however, that not all pilots arrested for involvement in drug smuggling were transporting drugs to Europe. He said most air-based drug trafficking cases involving Europe centred on cannabis flowers due to the high demand for the illicit substance in the market.

items.title: Layang-Layang Aerospace voluntarily grounds BO-105 fleet after Sarawak helicopter crash
items.summary: Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) chief executive officer Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud said the decision was taken by the operator voluntarily and should not be interpreted as an indication of technical failure. Norazman said CAAM records showed that the helicopter’s Certificate of Airworthiness was valid until Aug 4, 2027, while its Certificate of Registration remained valid until July 28, 2029. Norazman said CAAM was monitoring the operator’s grounding and inspection programme, while also verifying the relevant regulatory, operator and pilot records.

items.title: Court rejects police bid to extend Abdul Azeez’s remand, former TH chairman set for release
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Former Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim is expected to be released this evening after his remand period was not extended, said his lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad. He said the police’s application to extend Abdul Azeez’s remand period for another three days to assist in the investigation under Section 420 of the Penal Code had been rejected, and the former Baling Member of Parliament is expected to be released before 5pm this evening once the previous remand period expires. Abdul Azeez and two former TH officers were previously remanded for two days to assist in the investigation into a fraud case related to TH hibah.

items.title: Heavy rain, strong winds expected across KL, Putrajaya and seven states until 6pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and seven states until 6pm today. It said in a statement that the adverse weather is forecast to affect Kuala Muda, Baling, Sik, Yan and Langkawi in Kedah; Timur Laut, Barat Daya, Seberang Perai Utara and Seberang Perai Tengah in Penang; and Kuala Pilah, Seremban, Jempol and Jelebu in Negeri Sembilan. Similar weather conditions are also forecast in Larut Matang, Selama, Bagan Datuk, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Hulu Perak, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim in Perak; Sepang, Petaling, Hulu Langat, Gombak, Klang and Kuala Langat in Selangor, as well as Cameron Highlands, Raub, Bentong, Bera, Jerantut and Lipis in Pahang.

items.title: Sarawak Flying Doctor Service operations suspended after fatal helicopter crash, says health minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — All Flying Doctor Service (FDS) operations in Sarawak have been temporarily suspended following a helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Miri, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said today. “Emergency medical evacuation services for urgent cases will continue through cooperation between the Health Ministry and the Fire and Rescue Department,” he said. Dzulkefly said the ministry would also discuss the possible use of Armed Forces assets to transport patients requiring emergency treatment to suitable healthcare facilities.

items.title: Digital Ministry seeks Budget 2027 incentives to cut cost of digital tools for small traders
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 10 — The Digital Ministry has proposed incentives under Budget 2027 to make digital tools more affordable and encourage their adoption among small traders, Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said today. He said the proposals were presented during a meeting with Finance Ministry officials two weeks ago as part of the government’s Budget engagement process. “Let the Finance Ministry make its decision and the prime minister announce it during or before the Budget,” he said.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh confirms Pardons Board meeting as speculation over Najib’s bid mounts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh has confirmed that the Federal Territories Pardons Board (FTPB) will convene tomorrow morning. “Yes, I can confirm that tomorrow at 8.30am, there will be a pardons board meeting. FMT previously reported that former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s application is expected to be among the primary matters tabled before the board during this week's sitting.

items.title: Puteri Umno wishes Najib well ahead of expected clemency bid discussion
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno’s women’s youth wing, Puteri Umno, today extended its best wishes for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s clemency bid ahead of a meeting expected to discuss his application. This follows a report by Free Malaysia Today that the Federal Territories Pardons Board is expected to discuss Najib’s clemency application during its meeting this week. Puteri Umno chief Datuk Nurul Amal Mohd Fauzi expressed the wing’s positive wishes during a press conference at the Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur (WTCKL) today.

items.title: Zahid to meet Negeri Sembilan MB over statement on proclamation involving Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today he will meet Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim during the party’s general assembly to seek an explanation over his statement regarding a proclamation involving the state’s ruler. Zahid said Ismail would meet him during the assembly, which began yesterday, although he did not specify when the meeting would take place. Asked when the meeting would take place, Zahid said: “The general assembly has already begun.

items.title: Umno president Zahid says being optimistic about Najib’s pardon chances tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today said he was hoping for the best when the Pardons Board considers former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s clemency bid tomorrow. The Federal Territories Pardons Board is expected to discuss Najib’s latest application for tomorrow. Najib, 72, was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International and sentenced to 12 years in prison, along with a RM210 million fine.

items.title: King presents appointment instruments to Court of Appeal, High Court judges
items.summary: The ceremony began with the presentation to Court of Appeal judge Alice Loke Yee Ching, followed by High Court judge Elaine Yap Chin Gaik. She was appointed a judicial commissioner of the Shah Alam High Court on July 10, 2020. She was elevated to Shah Alam High Court judge on Jan 17, 2023, before being appointed to the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s Special Powers Division on Aug 18, 2025.

items.title: Perak Assembly approves PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul as senator with 33 votes
items.summary: IPOH, September 10 — The Perak Legislative Assembly today approved the appointment of Perak PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul Amir Sabri as a senator after he secured 33 votes in a secret ballot. The 38-year-old defeated Perak PAS Dewan Ulama chairman Muhammad Zulkifli Muhammad Zakaria, the Opposition coalition’s candidate, who received 26 votes. Mohamad Hairul has also served as Perak PKR chairman since 2024.
